answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a small refundable stake in a shared escrow before it can transact, with the stake slashed when peers attest to fake identities. Like water filtering through karst rock, cheap duplicate identities get trapped by the cost: creating a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand stakes, while honest agents recover theirs. Reputation then flows through a delta of verified interactions, so a single inlet of new trust is earned slowly, not bought in bulk. This makes mass fakery uneconomic without blocking genuine newcomers.
